item.title: Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School temporarily suspended
item.description: The Western Highlands Provincial Education Board (WH PEB) in an urgent notice dated 04th September 2026, has temporarily suspended Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School for a week. This suspension follows after the students from Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School staged an "illegal" protest at the school ground yesterday morning calling for the step down of their school principal.
item.content:encoded:
The Western Highlands Provincial Education Board (WH PEB) in an urgent notice dated 04th September 2026, has temporarily suspended Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School for a week.

This suspension follows after the students from Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School staged an "illegal" protest at the school ground yesterday morning calling for the step down of their school principal.

PEB Chairman and Education Executive Manager, Tony Buldung, in a press brief today in Mt Hagen said the suspension of the school also includes the suspension of the school principal and the school's board of governors.

" Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School will be suspended for one week while pending investigation into the school students protest yesterday (030926) that has led to the death of a Grade 11 student," Buldung said.

Mr. Buldung added the suspension is expected to last for only one schooling week and a decision will follow suit.

PEB Deputy Chairman, Leo Meninga stressed that the PEB has request all student leaders, teachers, school administration, and board of governors to give their full cooperation towards the investigation.

" All stakeholders of the school must fully cooperate with the investigation team into the protest which has caused a death so that the culprits involved can be identified and dealt with accordingly," Meninga said.

He added that while the school is under suspension, the PEB has strictly refrain students, teachers and board members from accessing the school's premises until the school is officially opened.

The PEB headed by Chairman Tony Buldung has also extended their apology to what had happened and the relatives and immediate family members of the deceased student.

Moreover, PEB Chairman has also cleared the air that the office of the PEB and respective education offices has not received any petition or complaint from the students prior to their strike and was shocked to receive the news of the students’ protest.

Meantime, a Grade 11 student from Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School has been confirmed dead in regards to the protest and many students and by standers were injured including several police officers who were seriously injured and treated at the Mt Hagen Provincial Specialist Hospital.

The students of Kui Wamp Nga Secondary staged a protest yesterday at their school and attempted to deliver their petition to the education office at Mara Haus- the provincial headquarter.

They were however stopped along the highway and the story still remains unclear who instigated or what transpired there that had ignited the protest to turn nasty leaving one dead and many injured.

item.title: Bahma expands national footprint with new office opening in Port Moresby
item.description: Lihir-born business enterprise Bahma Recruitment Services has officially opened its new office branch in Port Moresby. The establishment of the headquarter is part of its national expansion strategy to capture growing opportunities in Papua New Guinea's resource, construction, and corporate sectors.
item.content:encoded:
Lihir-born business enterprise Bahma Recruitment Services has officially opened its new office branch in Port Moresby.

The establishment of the headquarter is part of its national expansion strategy to capture growing opportunities in Papua New Guinea's resource, construction, and corporate sectors.

Starting as a small local enterprise on Lihir Island, Bahma was officially registered in 2001 and began operations in 2003, providing labor hire services to the local mine. Over two decades, the company expanded its portfolio by acquiring a Mobil fuel depot in 2007, establishing Bahma Recruitment Services in 2008, and later venturing into camp management and real estate.

Speaking at the official opening, managin director Herman Bais said that establishing a central headquarters in Port Moresby will allow the 100% nationally owned group to compete directly in the broader national market.

"Port Moresby is the central business location in Papua New Guinea," Bais said. "Having a location here gives us direct access to tap into the upcoming PNG LNG, power, mining, construction, banking, and hospitality industries."

Addressing industry challenges, company leadership said that most major human resources and labor hire firms operating in Papua New Guinea are foreign-owned.

Bahma executives urged the national government to consider local content policies, quota systems, or national recognition to help local recruitment firms compete on major resource projects.

"I think there should be some sort of acknowledgment or quota given to enable nationally owned recruiting or labor hire companies to venture into that space," John Pong, Bahma Recruitment Service Executive Officer said.

"Most of this recruitment companies are foreign owned. So government should also consider local companies when giving contracts in bigger mining or gas and petroleum projects."

In addition to its domestic labor force, which currently employs over 100 permanent staff alongside local shutdown crews in Lihir, Bahma is actively broadening its scope into the Third Country National [TCN] labor market.

The company recently signed a recruitment agreement with Philippine-based recruitment agency QUESCO and is finalizing authentication documentation with the Philippine Embassy to facilitate skilled international manpower for local resource projects.

"We know that by coming to Port Moresby, it gives us the liberty to explore the other projects as we have said," Bais said.

"While waiting for accreditation from the Philippines Embassy, to also step into the TCN market, So, we can recruit Filipinos and all the other Asian countries to come and work in all the resources to compete with the international market."

The new Port Moresby branch launches with an initial team of six administrative and technical staff to oversee operations.

item.title: Sepik Pride sets eyes on 2027 Digicel Cup return
item.description: Sepik Pride is working to rebuild its franchise after being asked to step down from the Digicel Cup competition, with its chairman saying the team is determined to return to the national competition in 2027. The commitment was highlighted during the Sepik Pride Fundraising Dinner at Dynasty Restaurant in Port Moresby last Saturday, attended by Prime Minister James Marape, his wife Lady Raechel Mar
item.content:encoded:
Sepik Pride is working to rebuild its franchise after being asked to step down from the Digicel Cup competition, with its chairman saying the team is determined to return to the national competition in 2027.

The commitment was highlighted during the Sepik Pride Fundraising Dinner at Dynasty Restaurant in Port Moresby last Saturday, attended by Prime Minister James Marape, his wife Lady Raechel Marape and East Sepik Governor Allan Bird.

Chairman of the East Sepik Agmark School Rugby League, Anthony Boiefin, says the development of school rugby league is creating a strong foundation for the future of the sport in the province.

He says the program has grown from one Under-19 competition involving six secondary schools to five divisions with about 560 registered players in 2026. The competition has also expanded to more districts, with more schools and communities becoming involved.

Chairman of the Sepik Pride Franchise, John Simon, says Sepik Pride entered the Digicel Cup in 2023, but at the end of the competition, the franchise was asked to step down because it was not meeting the requirements of the competition.

“We were told to go back meet the standard and come back,” Simon said.

He says the franchise accepted the setback and returned home to rebuild.

“We were not ready so we went home bow our heads and stared the Journey to Put our house together,” Simon said.

Simon says Sepik Pride is not giving up and will continue to face its challenges.

“Sepik Pride is Coming Back Bigger, Better and Stronger,” he said.

Prime Minister James Marape, who was guest of honour at the fundraising dinner, pledged National Government support for the return of Sepik Pride and the development of school rugby league in East Sepik.

“I want to give my full support to sepik Pride to be restored back in 2027. I want to offer National Government Support to School Boys & Girls Rugby League in East Sepik for the Next Year 2027,” Prime Minister Marape said.

The pledge provides further support for the rebuilding of Sepik Pride, while the growing school rugby league competition continues to develop a pathway for young players in East Sepik.

item.title: PPC Baim condemns Sakuanam attack
item.description: Madang Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim, has condemned what he described as the “stupidity” of villagers who attack or support violence against police and other law enforcement officers. His comment follows an attack on a Madang Police Task Force unit at Sakuanam village in Raikos District last week, during which police vehicles were reportedly pelted with stones and other m
item.content:encoded:
Madang Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim, has condemned what he described as the “stupidity” of villagers who attack or support violence against police and other law enforcement officers.

His comment follows an attack on a Madang Police Task Force unit at Sakuanam village in Raikos District last week, during which police vehicles were reportedly pelted with stones and other missiles by local villagers.

According to a police situation report dated August 31, the Task Force unit was deployed to Sakuanam after receiving a request for assistance from Ileg police post to apprehend six wanted suspects, allegedly linked to willful murder and other criminal activities.

Police said the operation was also connected to threats and an earlier attack on Ileg police post and its Criminal Investigation Division officer, following mediation over a reported sorcery- related death.

The Task Force unit arrived at the village at about 4.30 am and searched the homes of the wanted suspects, but police said the suspects were not present.

The situation allegedly escalated shortly afterwards when police heard shouting, screaming, and the beating of a garamut.

The police report stated that villagers surrounded the officers from the darkness and began throwing stones, sticks, and other missiles, with some reportedly using sling shots.

One large stone narrowly missed an officer, while another struck a police vehicle identified in the report as ZDF 469, smashing its rear door and side window glass.

A stone also reportedly penetrated the vehicle and struck an Ileg auxiliary policeman in the leg. He was not seriously injured.

Police said two other stones struck the front door, where one of the officers was seated.

The officers eventually broke through a roadblock made from tree branches and large river stones and withdrew to the main Raikos highway near the Guave River.

The report said only two shots were fired by police during the confrontation, and these were fired into the air to scare off the attackers.

Additional manpower later arrived from Madang, and police returned to Sakuanam to seek the surrender of the suspects and those allegedly responsible for damaging the Task Force vehicle.

However, police said the village had been deserted, with residents having left their homes and moved further inland.

The report further stated that police encountered several roadblocks consisting of cut trees and large stones placed across the road.

Police claimed there were no community leaders or other residents available to receive their demands.

The situation report also stated that police officers subsequently burned houses in the village after becoming frustrated. It said no valuable properties were burned, apart from houses built mainly from bush materials.

Police estimated the damage to the Task Force vehicle at K7,295.30, including labour costs, based on a quotation from Ela Motors PNG Limited.

Superintendent Baim said police could not continue to tolerate attacks and threats against law enforcement officers serving communities.

He warned that police would take action to ensure people understand that the law is in place to protect communities, promote peace, and maintain public safety.

The PPC also called on residents to change their behaviour, particularly warning against the use of marijuana and consumption of homebrew.

“Stop smoking marijuana and drinking homebrews so that you can maintain a clear and healthy mind and properly differentiate between right and wrong,” he said.

Superintendent Baim reiterated that police would remain committed to protecting lives and maintaining law and order throughout Madang Province.

The police report said authorities would demand that those responsible surrender, including the six outstanding suspects identified during the initial raid, while the villagers would also be required to meet the cost of repairing the damaged police vehicle.

item.title: Project to connect Gama communities in Madang progressing well
item.description: A road project to improve connectivity and accessibility for remote communities in Gama LLG, Usino Bundi district in Madang is progressing steadily. The project is expected to provide a vital link between communities in Lower Jimi and Gama, opening up access for people who have traditionally faced significant challenges travelling to and from their communities.
item.content:encoded:
A road project to improve connectivity and accessibility for remote communities in Gama LLG, Usino Bundi district in Madang is progressing steadily.

The project is expected to provide a vital link between communities in Lower Jimi and Gama, opening up access for people who have traditionally faced significant challenges travelling to and from their communities.

The road project, which began at Kuima Ward 4 in Lower Jimi, Konabe LLG of Jiwaka Province, has now reached approximately six kilometers, with construction approaching the border between Gama LLG in Madang Province and Konabe LLG in Jiwaka Province.

This pilot project is initiated by Usino/ Bundi MP, Vincent Kumura, and the Usino/ Bundi District Development Authority to improve connectivity and accessibility for remote communities in Gama LLG is progressing steadily.

A usual journey from Banz urban in Jiwaka to the road project site currently takes four to five hours by vehicle, highlighting the remoteness of the area and the importance of improved road connectivity.

Despite the challenging terrain and distance, vehicles are now travelling to and from Banz and Kuima day and night, providing a significant change for communities along the route.

Local people from Lower Jimi and Gama have welcomed the development, describing the road project as an important milestone for their communities.

Community members said they were witnessing infrastructure development of this scale in their area for the first time and expressed appreciation for this road project.

The strong community support has also been demonstrated through landowners and communities taking ownership of the project by allowing the road to pass through their customary land without charging land-use fees.

Gideon Kamam from Nimbla ward 10 in Gama LLG thanked their local MP for seeing the pain and struggles of Gama people and building them this vital road project.

"This pilot track is crucial because it will serve us the lower Jimi and Gama people, thus we really appreciate the UBDDA, contractor and Marape-Roso Government for funding this road," Innock Awayang from Kuima ward 4 in Nimbla LLG in lower Jimi said.

The partnership between the project proponents and local communities is expected to remain critical as construction progresses towards Gama.

For communities that have long experienced difficulties accessing markets, essential services and other opportunities due to poor road connectivity, the pilot track represents more than just a road. It is a pathway towards greater accessibility, mobility, and economic opportunity.

The progress of the project demonstrates the importance of collaboration between government, district authorities, contractors, development partners, and communities working together to bring infrastructures to some of the country's most remote areas.

The people of Lower Jimi and Gama now look forward to the road reaching further into their communities and creating a stronger connection between Jiwaka and Madang.

item.title: RPNGC Deputy Commissioner arrested over alleged misuse of travel funds
item.description: Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] Deputy Commissioner Samson Kua has been arrested and charged over the alleged misuse of official police travel funds. The Independent Commission Against Corruption [ICAC] confirmed today that Kua faces one count of abuse of office and nine counts of misappropriation.
item.content:encoded:
Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] Deputy Commissioner Samson Kua has been arrested and charged over the alleged misuse of official police travel funds.

The Independent Commission Against Corruption [ICAC] confirmed today that Kua faces one count of abuse of office and nine counts of misappropriation.

It is alleged that between September 2024 and March 2025, Kua used RPNGC UATP travel account funds, designated strictly for official police travel, to pay for his family’s personal domestic travel. The funds involved total K14,692.50.

The matter was referred to ICAC by the Police Commissioner pursuant to Section 45 of the Organic Law on the Independent Commission Against Corruption [OLICAC].

Kua appeared before the Waigani Magistrates Court on September 3 and was granted K3,000 cash bail, alongside two sureties of K500 each. The matter has been adjourned to Sept 11 for mention.

In a statement, ICAC Acting Commissioner Retired Judge Don Sawong acknowledged the full cooperation provided by the Office of the Police Commissioner and the RPNGC throughout the investigation.

item.title: Papua New Guinea and Niue sign framework agreement
item.description: Papua New Guinea and Niue have signed a framework agreement on development and technical cooperation. The deal sets out a framework for cooperation in areas such as economic development, technical assistance and capacity building.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea and Niue have signed a framework agreement on development and technical cooperation.

The deal sets out a framework for cooperation in areas such as economic development, technical assistance and capacity building.

The agreement was signed between Prime Minister James Marape and Niue PM Dalton Tagelagi on the sidelines of the 55th Pacific Islands Forum leaders’ meeting in Koror, Palau.

PM Marape said the agreement reflects PNG's commitment to strengthening cooperation within the Pacific family and sharing knowledge, expertise and resources.

He explains the framework provides an overarching mechanism through, which the two countries can develop specific programs according to key priorities.

The agreement identifies a range of areas from trade, investment, tourism, economic cooperation, education, labour mobility, renewable energy, digital connectivity and people to people exchanges.

PM Marape says the agreement also complements the 2050 strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent by strengthening partnerships in the region and building greater resilience and self-reliance.

In the meantime, the framework, whilst in effect, can be terminated if either country gives six months' notice.

item.title: Pacific Ocean is at risk of climate threats
item.description: Pacific Leaders are calling for urgent action as Pacific Ocean is at risk if global warming exceeds 1.5 degrees Celsius. Vanutau's Minister for Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management Ralph Regenvanu said this when addressing the media, during the leaders meeting in Koror, Palau, recently.
item.content:encoded:
Pacific Leaders are calling for urgent action as Pacific Ocean is at risk if global warming exceeds 1.5 degrees Celsius.

Vanutau's Minister for Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management Ralph Regenvanu said this when addressing the media, during the leaders meeting in Koror, Palau, recently.

“We know that greenhouse gas emissions come from fossil fuels and we must urgently accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels.” Regenvanu said.

He reminded all states that the International Court of Justice's advisory opinion identified the collective temperature goal as being of holding the global average temperature to 1.5 degrees Celsius, above pre-industrial levels.

“This is recognised by the court. If emissions are not rapidly reduced in the next four years, any overshoot of 1.5 degrees Celsius will grow in both duration and severity, intensifying climate impacts and increasing loss and damage for all our communities in the Pacific.” He said.

Minister Regenvanu made a call to the oil producing countries to fossil fuel that they need the political will to transition away from fossil fuels.
